title: Know what each input means
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Know what each input means. Define: The square belongs to the generator, not a discovery from test labels. Walk through: The fixed rule is y=2*x0+x1 squared+noise. Each independent row has an ID and a saved split. No physical input units are invented. Ask: Does knowing the generator justify choosing on the test score? Expected answer and boundary: No. It justifies predeclaring this teaching comparison. The winner is still chosen by the declared validation MAE rule. Visual purpose: show x0: linear signal | x1: squared signal | x2: negative control. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Separate fitting, choosing and evaluating
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Separate fitting, choosing and evaluating. Define: Only training rows fit scaler and model parameters. Walk through: Check 350/75/75 rows, disjoint IDs and the frozen CSV hash. Then fit both training-only pipelines; exact validation ties favor the linear candidate. Ask: What would fitting the scaler on all rows change? Expected answer and boundary: It would let held-out inputs influence a fitted preprocessing step.
